name: pledge to the elements

attributes.attribute: calls air, sea, and earth to witness
shows the world alive and watchful

sources: Cowan, Tom. “The Pledge to the Elements.” In Patricia Monaghan, ed. Irish Spirit: Pagan, Celtic, Christian, Global. Dublin: Wolfhound Press, 2001.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The pledge to the elements is a Continental Celtic ritual. In Gaul an oath is taken with these words: may the skies fall on me, the seas drown me, and the earth swallow me whole. The pledge calls on the air, sea, and earth to witness the speaker's truth. It shows the Celtic view that the world is alive and watchful.

okr.objective: Present the pledge to the elements as a lived Celtic oath.
key_results: quotes the sky, sea, and earth oath of Gaul
calls the world alive and watchful
records it as a Continental Celtic rite
